pathway.title: ENTEGRIS INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The first finding is that Entegris, Inc. has deleveraged on both sides of the ratio. Par debt fell to USD 3,295.0 million at September 26, 2026 from USD 3,745.0 million at December 31, 2025 through term loan repayment of USD 450.0 million, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,008.2 million from USD 886.2 million in FY2025, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x at FY2024 to 4.23x at FY2025 and 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 3.99x to 3.82x to 2.91x. The mechanism is repayment from operating cash flow, which also removed floating-rate exposure, so the remaining debt service is fixed coupons of about USD 161.3 million a year and cash interest cover is 5.57x. [CP-1 leverage and interest cover data, debt schedule]

The second finding is that the cash generation behind this is strong but partly timing-supported. LTM free cash flow after capital spending was USD 616.0 million, equal to 18.7% of par debt, helped by capital spending of USD 182.0 million LTM against USD 299.2 million in FY2025 and by a working-capital inflow from payables and incentive accruals that the filings describe as timing. If capital spending returns toward the roughly USD 250.0 million planned in the annual report, or payables normalise, free cash flow would fall. [CP-1 financials and cash flow quality]

The third finding is that liquidity is ample and the maturity profile is back-ended but concentrated. Cash of USD 356.5 million plus the undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver gives USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, which are not supplied, and the revolver runs to April 29, 2031. Maturities are nil to 2027, USD 400.0 million in 2028, USD 2,000.0 million in 2029 (60.7% of par debt, including the USD 1,600.0 million secured notes) and USD 895.0 million in 2030, so refinancing risk sits in 2029 and depends on market access then. Only USD 58.3 million of the cash is held in the U.S. [CP-1 liquidity and debt maturities]

The fourth finding is that business risk is the weak side of the credit. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company was 16% of FY2025 net sales and the top ten customers were 50%; customers provide non-binding forecasts and no long-term purchase commitments. In Q3 2026 net sales rose 24.6% year on year, mainly on volume, but sales to Equipment and Engineering customers rose 66.8% against 19.3% for fabs, so part of the growth follows equipment shipments, which are more cyclical. A volume reversal would hit operating leverage first and then cash flow and leverage. [CP-1A operating model]

The fifth finding is that reported 2026 profitability flatters the run-rate. Depreciation was USD 55.6 million lower over nine months 2026 from a change in useful lives, and USD 8.3 million of tariff refunds helped Q3 2026 gross margin, though both are excluded from or neutral to Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined; on unadjusted EBITDA, total leverage is 3.36x LTM Q3 2026 against 3.27x, so definition risk is small today. Covenant EBITDA is not supplied: the first lien net leverage covenant of 5.20x, tested only when revolver utilisation exceeds a threshold that is not printed, cannot be compared with any ratio, and a purely illustrative first lien net leverage of 1.23x (secured notes less cash over Adjusted EBITDA) is not covenant headroom. [CP-1 definition review, covenants]

The sixth finding concerns creditor control. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is identified, dividends are a steady USD 0.10 per share each quarter, there were no buybacks in FY2025, and the documented actions are debt repayment, so no extraction behaviour is documented. The legal capacity to add secured debt is wide in principle, with incremental amounts up to the greater of USD 1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA, and the financing documents, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so structural priority and any creditor-protection conclusion are left open. [CP-1A governance and capital allocation]

runs.text: Strengths. Debt reduction with falling leverage is a documented fact: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, down from 4.34x at FY2024, with all remaining debt fixed-rate notes and no maturity before 2028 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 leverage data and debt schedule). Cash generation is strong: LTM free cash flow of USD 616.0 million exceeds the sum of the roughly USD 161.3 million of annual note coupons and LTM dividends of USD 61.3 million, which is USD 222.6 million, by USD 393.4 million (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 cash flow figures; the coupon figure excludes revolver fees). Liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, with no facility expiring within twelve months, gives room to absorb a downturn (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the sum excludes unsupplied letters of credit). The business is embedded in customer processes through recurring consumables and no platform exceeds 3% of net sales, which management describes as supporting revenue that is predominantly unit-driven or recurring (Management Language; basis CP-1A operating model). Capital allocation is creditor-friendly on documented actions: debt repayment, steady dividends and no repurchases, with no sponsor (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance).

Weaknesses. Revenue is concentrated and uncommitted: one customer is 16% of FY2025 sales and ten customers are 50%, with no long-term purchase commitments (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A customers). Demand is cyclical and the recent growth leans on equipment-linked categories, which may reverse (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A end markets). Earnings quality needs care: depreciation was reduced by an accounting estimate change, tariff refunds were one-off, Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and covenant EBITDA is unknown (Documentary Fact for the items; Analyst Interpretation for the effect). Refinancing is concentrated in 2029, at USD 2,000.0 million or 60.7% of par debt (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 debt maturities). Supply and trade exposure is real: single-source inputs, 26% of Q3 2026 sales to Taiwan and flat sales to China (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A operating model). Contract, covenant, letter-of-credit, guarantor and rating evidence is Not supplied, so headroom, structural priority and market view cannot be assessed (Insufficient Information; the missing items would decide covenant and structural conclusions).

runs.text: There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition, merger, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the supplied sources for 2026, and none is announced by the as-of date. The financing events in 2026 are two. First, on April 29, 2026 the company amended its senior secured revolving credit facility to raise commitments to $750.0 million from $575.0 million, extend the maturity to April 29, 2031 from July 6, 2027, and revise margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants (Q3 10-Q page:12, page:22); the revised negative covenants are not described, and the amendment itself is not supplied. Second, the company repaid the term loans B in full during 2026 (50.0 in the first quarter, 200.0 in the second and 200.0 in the third, including a voluntary 25 on July 31, 2026), so that outstanding principal is now only fixed-rate notes of $3,295.0 million and an undrawn revolver (Q1 10-Q page:11; Q2 10-Q page:12, page:17; Q3 10-Q page:11, page:12). Cash flow statements for the nine months show repayments of $450.0 million and no proceeds from new long-term debt (Q3 10-Q page:7); the revolver was borrowed and repaid at 65.0 during the period. For use of proceeds and liquidity effect, the repayments were funded from operating cash flow of $606.0 million over nine months and reduced cash by little (cash $356.5 million against $360.4 million at December 31, 2025). Earlier history that shaped the balance sheet: the CMC Materials acquisition closed in July 2022 and was financed under the July 2022 credit agreement amendment and indenture supplements listed as exhibits (10-K page:5, page:97); debt payments of $848.3 million against proceeds of $224.5 million in FY2024 and payments of $300.0 million in FY2025 came after the asset sales listed in the timeline (10-K page:108). The nature of the FY2024 long-term debt proceeds is not described in the pack beyond a third amendment of the term loan facility in 2024 (10-K page:76, page:98). The dividend declared on October 14, 2026 ($0.10 per share, payable November 18, 2026) is a subsequent event after the quarter end (Q3 10-Q page:17). Management's Capital Markets Day on November 9, 2026 is a future event after the as-of date and no content from it is available (Q3 release page:1).

First, its gap G8 said the fourth quarter of 2025 is not presented on its own. The Q1 release does print a discrete column for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (net sales $823.9, Adjusted EBITDA $228.1; `Q1 release page:5`, `page:7`), and it agrees with the figure derived from the annual and nine-month numbers (see Calculations, C1). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the limits stated below. Everything rests on filed, consolidated statements of Entegris, Inc. and subsidiaries in USD millions, supplemented by the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which the filings reconcile to GAAP. On that basis, principal debt fell from $4,045.0 at FY2024 to $3,745.0 at FY2025 and $3,295.0 at September 26, 2026, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from $886.2 (FY2025) to $1,008.2, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x to 4.23x to 3.27x. The nine-month 2026 debt reduction is entirely term loan B repayment of $450.0; every remaining instrument is a fixed-rate note, the revolver is undrawn, and maturities start in 2028. Interest cover on cash interest paid is 5.57x LTM. Three things restrict the view. First, Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and the covenant definition is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable; the filing states compliance and a 5.20 to 1.00 first lien net leverage maximum that is tested only above a revolver utilisation threshold that is not printed. Second, letters of credit under the revolver are not supplied, so undrawn availability is shown before them. Third, 2026 operating income and margin are not like-for-like with 2025 because of the January 2026 change in useful lives, while Adjusted EBITDA adds depreciation back and is unaffected by it. The annual report's thousands captions on millions amounts are a known unit-label conflict, resolved by the Q3 10-Q statement that amounts are in millions (`10-K page:120`, `Q3 10-Q page:9`).

fields.value: Net sales in Q3 2026 are the highest of the seven quarters shown, and Adjusted EBITDA margin rose in each 2026 quarter shown (27.8%, 28.4%, 30.2%). Management calls the quarter "record revenue" (`Q3 release page:1`); that is attributed management language and is not tested against quarters outside the pack. Year on year, Q3 net sales rose 24.6% from 807.1 to 1,005.7, which the 10-Q attributes primarily to volume of 205.8 (`Q3 10-Q page:23`).

Unallocated general and administrative expense was 62.7 in FY2025 and 60.3 in nine months 2026 (`10-K page:77`; `Q3 10-Q page:15`). Advanced Purity Solutions segment profit rose from 322.2 to 497.2 over nine months, against sales growth from 1,334.6 to 1,583.1; the 10-Q attributes the profit increase to higher gross profit on higher sales, lower depreciation from the useful-life change and tariff refunds, partly offset by variable compensation (`Q3 10-Q page:31`).

The sources print no co-issuers, no guarantor amounts and no month of maturity for the notes; the equal priority intercreditor agreement among the credit facility and notes collateral agents is listed as an exhibit (`10-K page:97`), which indicates equal-priority liens but is not a term the pack documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit agreement for the revolver and term loan (the "Amended Credit Agreement") contains a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.20 to 1.00, tested only when utilisation of the revolver exceeds a specified threshold; the company states compliance through September 26, 2026 (`Q3 10-Q page:34`; same wording in `Q2 10-Q page:31`; `Q1 10-Q page:28` states compliance without a level). The threshold is not printed, the reported ratio is not printed, and no step-down is described. The revolver margin tiers depend on the same first lien net leverage ratio, and the margin fell from 1.50% (SOFR) at June 27, 2026 to 1.25% at September 26, 2026 (`Q2 10-Q page:12`; `Q3 10-Q page:12`), which is consistent with improving first lien leverage but does not give the ratio. An illustrative figure only: if the 1,600.0 secured notes are first lien debt and cash is fully netted, first lien net debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 1.23x (C8); the covenant definition of debt, cash netting and EBITDA are not supplied, so this is not covenant headroom and no headroom is stated. Other restrictions are summarised in the annual report risk factors: restrictions on debt, dividends, investments, liens and asset sales, and incremental capacity up to the greater of $1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA plus amounts subject to a secured net leverage test (`10-K page:54`); the indentures carry limited covenants on secured debt, sale-leasebacks and restricted subsidiary debt (`10-K page:56`).

fields.value: The business context is usable, with a clear picture of what the company does and a thin picture of who owns it and what it has contracted. Entegris sells consumable materials and purity equipment into semiconductor fabrication through two segments, Materials Solutions and Advanced Purity Solutions, and describes its revenue as predominantly unit-driven or recurring (management language, `10-K page:9`). The mechanism that matters to a creditor is demand linkage: sales follow wafer starts and fab build-outs, a few very large customers account for half of sales, and customers carry no long-term purchase commitments, so revenue visibility is short and a cut in one customer's capital plan transmits quickly into volume, operating leverage and debt service. The latest quarter shows the upside of that link: Q3 2026 net sales grew 24.6% on volume, but the equipment-linked customer category grew far faster than fabs, which is the more cyclical part of the mix. On ownership and transactions, the pack shows a publicly traded company with 907 holders of record, no sponsor, no parent, no acquisition disclosed and no new debt issue; the transaction history is a portfolio clean-up between 2023 and 2025 whose asset sales coincided with large debt repayments, and the 2026 financing events are an amended revolver and repayment of the term loan from cash flow. What the pack cannot show is who the large holders are, what the financing documents permit beyond summaries, and how the company is rated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition, merger, recapitalisation or new debt issue in the supplied sources for 2026, and none is announced by the as-of date. The financing events in 2026 are two. First, on April 29, 2026 the company amended its senior secured revolving credit facility to raise commitments to $750.0 million from $575.0 million, extend the maturity to April 29, 2031 from July 6, 2027, and revise margins, commitment fees and certain negative covenants (`Q3 10-Q page:12`, `page:22`); the revised negative covenants are not described, and the amendment itself is not supplied. Second, the company repaid the term loans B in full during 2026 (50.0 in the first quarter, 200.0 in the second and 200.0 in the third, including a voluntary 25 on July 31, 2026), so that outstanding principal is now only fixed-rate notes of $3,295.0 million and an undrawn revolver (`Q1 10-Q page:11`; `Q2 10-Q page:12`, `page:17`; `Q3 10-Q page:11`, `page:12`). Cash flow statements for the nine months show repayments of $450.0 million and no proceeds from new long-term debt (`Q3 10-Q page:7`); the revolver was borrowed and repaid at 65.0 during the period. For use of proceeds and liquidity effect, the repayments were funded from operating cash flow of $606.0 million over nine months and reduced cash by little (cash $356.5 million against $360.4 million at December 31, 2025). Earlier history that shaped the balance sheet: the CMC Materials acquisition closed in July 2022 and was financed under the July 2022 credit agreement amendment and indenture supplements listed as exhibits (`10-K page:5`, `page:97`); debt payments of $848.3 million against proceeds of $224.5 million in FY2024 and payments of $300.0 million in FY2025 came after the asset sales listed in the timeline (`10-K page:108`). The nature of the FY2024 long-term debt proceeds is not described in the pack beyond a third amendment of the term loan facility in 2024 (`10-K page:76`, `page:98`). The dividend declared on October 14, 2026 ($0.10 per share, payable November 18, 2026) is a subsequent event after the quarter end (`Q3 10-Q page:17`). Management's Capital Markets Day on November 9, 2026 is a future event after the as-of date and no content from it is available (`Q3 release page:1`).

fields.value: Entegris, Inc. is a cyclical, customer-concentrated supplier of semiconductor materials whose credit profile improved sharply in 2026 and is now adequate for its debt load. The strongest support is deleveraging with cash generation: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x on an LTM Q3 2026 basis against 4.23x for FY2025, the term loan has been repaid, the remaining USD 3,295.0 million of debt is fixed-rate notes, and nothing matures before 2028. The weakest point is the quality and durability of earnings: demand is volume-led from a few very large customers with no purchase commitments, and 2026 margins are helped by an accounting change and one-off refunds. What decides the outcome is whether advanced logic and memory fab demand holds through the 2028 to 2030 maturities. [CP-1 leverage data; CP-1A operating model]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first finding is that Entegris, Inc. has deleveraged on both sides of the ratio. Par debt fell to USD 3,295.0 million at September 26, 2026 from USD 3,745.0 million at December 31, 2025 through term loan repayment of USD 450.0 million, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,008.2 million from USD 886.2 million in FY2025, so total debt over Adjusted EBITDA moved from 4.34x at FY2024 to 4.23x at FY2025 and 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA from 3.99x to 3.82x to 2.91x. The mechanism is repayment from operating cash flow, which also removed floating-rate exposure, so the remaining debt service is fixed coupons of about USD 161.3 million a year and cash interest cover is 5.57x. [CP-1 leverage and interest cover data, debt schedule]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second finding is that the cash generation behind this is strong but partly timing-supported. LTM free cash flow after capital spending was USD 616.0 million, equal to 18.7% of par debt, helped by capital spending of USD 182.0 million LTM against USD 299.2 million in FY2025 and by a working-capital inflow from payables and incentive accruals that the filings describe as timing. If capital spending returns toward the roughly USD 250.0 million planned in the annual report, or payables normalise, free cash flow would fall. [CP-1 financials and cash flow quality]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third finding is that liquidity is ample and the maturity profile is back-ended but concentrated. Cash of USD 356.5 million plus the undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver gives USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, which are not supplied, and the revolver runs to April 29, 2031. Maturities are nil to 2027, USD 400.0 million in 2028, USD 2,000.0 million in 2029 (60.7% of par debt, including the USD 1,600.0 million secured notes) and USD 895.0 million in 2030, so refinancing risk sits in 2029 and depends on market access then. Only USD 58.3 million of the cash is held in the U.S. [CP-1 liquidity and debt maturities]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth finding is that business risk is the weak side of the credit. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company was 16% of FY2025 net sales and the top ten customers were 50%; customers provide non-binding forecasts and no long-term purchase commitments. In Q3 2026 net sales rose 24.6% year on year, mainly on volume, but sales to Equipment and Engineering customers rose 66.8% against 19.3% for fabs, so part of the growth follows equipment shipments, which are more cyclical. A volume reversal would hit operating leverage first and then cash flow and leverage. [CP-1A operating model]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth finding is that reported 2026 profitability flatters the run-rate. Depreciation was USD 55.6 million lower over nine months 2026 from a change in useful lives, and USD 8.3 million of tariff refunds helped Q3 2026 gross margin, though both are excluded from or neutral to Adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined; on unadjusted EBITDA, total leverage is 3.36x LTM Q3 2026 against 3.27x, so definition risk is small today. Covenant EBITDA is not supplied: the first lien net leverage covenant of 5.20x, tested only when revolver utilisation exceeds a threshold that is not printed, cannot be compared with any ratio, and a purely illustrative first lien net leverage of 1.23x (secured notes less cash over Adjusted EBITDA) is not covenant headroom. [CP-1 definition review, covenants]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sixth finding concerns creditor control. No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is identified, dividends are a steady USD 0.10 per share each quarter, there were no buybacks in FY2025, and the documented actions are debt repayment, so no extraction behaviour is documented. The legal capacity to add secured debt is wide in principle, with incremental amounts up to the greater of USD 1.1 billion or 100% of EBITDA, and the financing documents, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so structural priority and any creditor-protection conclusion are left open. [CP-1A governance and capital allocation]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Debt reduction with falling leverage is a documented fact: total debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 3.27x LTM Q3 2026, down from 4.34x at FY2024, with all remaining debt fixed-rate notes and no maturity before 2028 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 leverage data and debt schedule). Cash generation is strong: LTM free cash flow of USD 616.0 million exceeds the sum of the roughly USD 161.3 million of annual note coupons and LTM dividends of USD 61.3 million, which is USD 222.6 million, by USD 393.4 million (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 cash flow figures; the coupon figure excludes revolver fees). Liquidity of USD 1,106.5 million before letters of credit, with no facility expiring within twelve months, gives room to absorb a downturn (Documentary Fact for the inputs; the sum excludes unsupplied letters of credit). The business is embedded in customer processes through recurring consumables and no platform exceeds 3% of net sales, which management describes as supporting revenue that is predominantly unit-driven or recurring (Management Language; basis CP-1A operating model). Capital allocation is creditor-friendly on documented actions: debt repayment, steady dividends and no repurchases, with no sponsor (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Revenue is concentrated and uncommitted: one customer is 16% of FY2025 sales and ten customers are 50%, with no long-term purchase commitments (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A customers). Demand is cyclical and the recent growth leans on equipment-linked categories, which may reverse (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A end markets). Earnings quality needs care: depreciation was reduced by an accounting estimate change, tariff refunds were one-off, Adjusted EBITDA is management-defined and covenant EBITDA is unknown (Documentary Fact for the items; Analyst Interpretation for the effect). Refinancing is concentrated in 2029, at USD 2,000.0 million or 60.7% of par debt (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 debt maturities). Supply and trade exposure is real: single-source inputs, 26% of Q3 2026 sales to Taiwan and flat sales to China (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A operating model). Contract, covenant, letter-of-credit, guarantor and rating evidence is Not supplied, so headroom, structural priority and market view cannot be assessed (Insufficient Information; the missing items would decide covenant and structural conclusions).
